chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'That the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled in the case of'

a man who bought a garment with a condition until midday; profit was presented to him, so he wanted to sell it. He (AS) said: 'Let him testify that he was pleased with it and it became obligatory upon him, then let him sell it if he wishes. If he kept it in the market and did not sell, then it has become obligatory upon him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on conditional sales and when does a sale become binding if the buyer delays?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the Shia juristic principle of *Khiyar al-Shart* (option of condition), clarifying that a conditional sale remains revocable until the buyer explicitly ratifies the transaction or the time limit expires. Imam Ali (AS) establishes that merely holding the item in the market without finalizing the sale does not constitute binding acceptance, thereby protecting the buyer from unintended obligation. This ruling underscores the importance of clear intent (*riḍā*) and the specific mechanics of conditional contracts in Islamic commercial law.
